reviewed.actor: The Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court (Chief Justice Rugg), 1931; the stored note says only "The court", so the label names it.
reviewed.scope: Massachusetts General Laws chapter 234, § 1, which made a person qualified to vote liable for jury service; read to cover only men, so women stayed off jury lists after they gained the vote.
reviewed.laterTreatment: None stored. The entry has no later-development line and the brief "does not certify its subsequent treatment". The label is in the past tense because the decision is dated 1931; it makes no claim that the rule changed.

supportingSentences.text: General Laws chapter 234, § 1 made a person qualified to vote for representatives to the General Court liable for jury service, subject to exceptions not material here.
In its view, the voter-based jury statute and its predecessors had always referred to men because the state constitution then confined voting to men.
The court thus held women ineligible under the existing statutes and approved preparation of all-male jury lists.
The Supreme Judicial Court addressed whether state law required otherwise-qualified women to be included on jury lists
The court read the jury-service statute in its historical setting and declined to extend it to women when they later gained voting rights.
